classification.difficultyReason: Expand reciprocal two-variable binomials and retain both original restrictions.

answer.short:
$xy+2+\frac{1}{xy}$, $x\ne0$ and $y\ne0$.

Expand the four products; the two middle products each equal $1$.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\left(x+\frac{1}{y}\right)\left(y+\frac{1}{x}\right)&=xy+\frac{x}{x}+\frac{y}{y}+\frac{1}{xy}\\\left(x+\frac{1}{y}\right)\left(y+\frac{1}{x}\right)&=xy+2+\frac{1}{xy}\end{align*}$$

$x\ne0$ and $y\ne0$, since both occur as denominators in the original expression.
